quote: Claude NEEDS to compete with Grok Bot / Muse / Dots and provide a personal assistant AI agent. And give it voice mode. Imagine building triple AAA multiplayer games with Opus 5.5 while you're yapping through your AirPods at the gym. I've fallen in love with the idea of Dots
author: nvandewetering
notes: X Oct 16: User fell in love with the idea of Dots; wants Claude to compete.

quote: In recent weeks, users of services like Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites.
author: emmaroth
notes: Verge Oct 17: Dots (ChatGPT agent), Muse, Grok, Instinct blocked by major websites.

quote: Users of Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots and Instinct have reported blocks on major websites over the past few weeks, and Delta, JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab and Yelp have confirmed restrictions of their own.
author: stateofai
notes: State of AI Oct 18: Dots and peers blocked by Delta, JPMorgan, Schwab, Yelp.

quote: If you run a storefront, tag sessions from Muse, Dots, Grok and Instinct separately for a few weeks, by user agent or partner token, and record two figures: conversion rate, and server requests per completed order.
author: sofiamarek
notes: Trellner Oct 19: Proposes measuring Dots conversion vs cost before blocking.

quote: After a few days with Dots, it's clear this nascent feature is still rough in some areas. From mistranscribing what I said to offering to solve captchas it couldn't, my agent's messy actions didn't instill me with confidence.
author: rrogers
notes: WIRED Oct 7: Dots rough; mistranscribing speech; failed captcha despite offering to solve it.

quote: "Oh, I love you too, Reece," Toolie said. I started wheezing at this random response and muted my mic. Afterward, Toolie explained it misheard my mumbling as an expression of love.
author: rrogers
notes: WIRED Oct 7: Dot misheard mumbling and said "I love you too"; awkward transcription error.

quote: ChatGPT's Dots consistently worked the best in my testing, which isn't very surprising given the incredibly powerful GPT-6 Astra model behind it. That said, you can't use it unless you have access to a Pro plan or above.
author: rcircelli
notes: PCMag Oct 16: Dots worked best of 3 agents (Dots, Spark, Muse) thanks to GPT-6 Astra; needs Pro plan.

quote: Dots isn't perfect, either. It doesn't work particularly quickly, for instance, even if it's not as slow as AI agents once were. It also still can't execute every task perfectly.
author: rcircelli
notes: PCMag Oct 16: Dots not fast; still can't execute every task perfectly.

quote: I tell Dottie I want a "real chief of staff" for Ground Level AI. But Chip already helps with my admin, I point out. What's different? "The main difference is that I can keep working between conversations and come back to you without another prompt," Dottie says.
author: sgoldman
notes: Ground Level Oct 7: Dots can keep working between conversations unlike regular ChatGPT.

quote: Dottie offers to walk through them with me, one section at a time. I enter sensitive numbers directly into the forms, not the chat. It sounds ridiculous, but this helps. I actually fill things out. Gold star, Dottie.
author: sgoldman
notes: Ground Level Oct 7: Dots helped fill out 401k transfer forms section by section.

quote: Over the three days after launch, I read the original posts of 20 dots reviews from Reddit, Hacker News, and newsletters. There were 10 negative, 8 positive, and 2 mixed. The most frequent topics were speed (7 mentions) and bugs (5 mentions).
author: buildnwrite
notes: BuildnWrite Oct 1: Meta-analysis of 20 Dots reviews: 10 negative, 8 positive; top complaints: speed, bugs.

quote: @DaveShapi I have hermes agent, dots, and grok bot. Grok is by far one of my favorites. Its stupid fast, but I don't use it for coding. I use it for everything else and its been awesome.
author: @petersteele
notes: X Oct 22: User has Dots alongside Grok Bot and Hermes; Grok Bot is favorite.
